html:
The Kongo-Wara rebellion was an uprising of the Gbaya and neighbouring peoples in the west of Ubangi-Shari and nearby Cameroon from 1928 to 1931, against forced labour and colonial rule.

It was inspired by a prophet named Karnou, who preached non-violence at first and gave followers small hoe-handle charms, the kongo wara, said to protect them. The trigger was the recruiting of men for the Congo to Ocean railway and the abuses of concession companies.

Karnou was killed in December 1928, but fighting went on in the forests for three years. The French crushed it and moved people into new villages. It was the largest revolt in interwar French Equatorial Africa, and Karnou is remembered as a national hero.
sum: The Kongo-Wara rebellion was an uprising of the Gbaya and neighbouring peoples in the west of Ubangi-Shari and nearby Cameroon from 1928 to 1931, against forced labour and colonial rule.
